subject: octopus
readings: Radially symmetric animal, no elongated head/tail: mantle (body sac) sits centered with eyes just markers, not a protruding head, so it is TRUNK not a leaf.
Arms spread widest and straightest in the XZ (top) panel -> XZ panel is the PROFILE for arm length/spread; XY and ZY panels show the same arms foreshortened by curling/drooping (droop = y).
Mantle: XY panel top of sac (12,9) vs arm-crown base (13,15) => mantle rises 6 units, so mantle direction = +y from arm base.
Dorsal-most (shortest) arm pair: XZ tip (4,3) vs base (13,12) => spread (-9,-9 on x,z-flip -> dz+9); XY tip y(8) vs base y(15) => rise +7. Direction ~ (-9,7,9)/(-9,7,-9) mirrored L/R.
Second arm pair: XZ tip (0,9ish) vs base (13,12); slightly less rise than pair1 in XY (~y11) => direction ~(-7,2,5)/(-7,2,-5).
Third arm pair: tips droop lower in XY (y~18-20) while XZ tip near (7,17-ish) relative to base => direction ~(-4,-6,6)/(-4,-6,-6).

Ventral-most (longest) arm pair: this is the arm that reaches the full 24-unit mark, defining the grid's longest extent. XZ tip (24,11) vs base (13,12) => dx=11, dz=1; XY tip y(11) vs base y(15) => dy=4. Direction ~(11,4,1)/(11,4,-1).
Eyes (two small dots near (13,11) in XY, and near center-top of head in ZY) are sub-flap detail, excluded from leaves per protocol.
No external tail or siphon-leaf identified; the pointed forward tip is simply the extended ventral arm pair, consistent across XY and XZ panels.
notes:
Octopus has a fused head/mantle (no neck-protruding head, so head is TRUNK not a leaf) and no external tail. Eight arms = eight leaves, grouped into four bilateral pairs (dorsal-most pair1, shortest, to ventral-most pair4, longest, matching real octopus arm-length gradient and matching the observed pose where one ventral arm is extended straight to the 24-unit mark). Each arm was split into two segments (base, tip) purely as an anatomical inference to allow the curling silhouette seen in all three panels; the raw mesh shows continuously curving arms rather than a distinct hinge, so segment directions were kept equal (straight) since no distinct bend landmark could be reliably read from the grid. Left/right assigned via the z-axis (ZY front panel), with +z taken as the animal's left. All four pairs attach to a single shared "mantle" trunk node, which is anatomically correct for an octopus (arms genuinely ring the single buccal mass) rather than being an erroneous shared-limb hub - each pair still has its own independent base->tip chain back to that spine node, never sharing a joint with its mirror partner.</notes>
